summary: Terraform runner unable to attach IAM role to instance profile during private deployment (permission boundary enforcement)
description: Issue summary: During a Private deployment (customer X onboarding), our terraform-runner fails when attempting to attach an IAM role to the EC2 instance profile. The AWS API returns AccessDenied with a note about a permission boundary. This appears after a recent org-wide permission-boundary propagation. Impact: Provisioning for one private customer environment is blocked; dedicated/nodepool creation for private deploys is failing and CI runs are stuck. Environment: prod account for private-deploy-us-east, terraform-runner job v2026.03.09, org permission-boundary recently updated (deploy-priv-boundary-v2).
impact: Private deployment provisioning blocked for one onboarding customer; manual workarounds required for other pending customers. CI job queue for private deploys is growing and dedicated capacity allocation is delayed.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Kick off private deployment pipeline for customer X (pipeline: private-deploy/provision) using terraform-runner v2026.03.09
2) Terraform applies resources: create instance profile, create role, attempt aws_iam_role_policy_attachment and aws_iam_instance_profile_role attachment
3) aws API returns AccessDenied when attaching role to instance profile with error referencing permission boundary 'deploy-priv-boundary-v2'
4) Pipeline errors out and keeps the terraform workspace locked; further retries fail with same error
logs: aws iam attach-role-policy --role-name rw-priv-deploy-ec2-role --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AmazonEC2RoleforSSM ERROR: AccessDenied: User: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/terraform-runner-role/terraform is not authorized to perform: iam:AttachRolePolicy on resource: role rw-priv-deploy-ec2-role due to permission boundary: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:policy/deploy-priv-boundary-v2
Terraform apply log snippet: Error: Error attaching IAM Role to Instance Profile: AccessDenied: Cannot call PutRolePolicy on role rw-priv-deploy-ec2-role: Permission boundary prevents operation
CloudTrail event id: 9a1b2c3d-logs: iam:PutRolePolicy denied by policy deploy-priv-boundary-v2 (principal: terraform-runner-sa)
Recent org change: PR #2754 merged 2026-03-08: 'enforce-deploy-boundary-v2' applied across prod accounts
investigation_notes: Checked CloudTrail events for the failing request (event IDs above). The denied action is iam:AttachRolePolicy / iam:PassRole when called by terraform-runner assumed role.

Confirmed permission boundary 'deploy-priv-boundary-v2' was applied org-wide on 2026-03-08 (related PR). The boundary restricts allowed IAM actions and principals; its current statement blocks attaching managed policies unless the request includes a specific tag 'trusted-deployer=true'.

Observed terraform-runner assumes role 'terraform-runner-role' that does not include the required tag in the request context; AWS does not accept request context tags for iam:AttachRolePolicy in our current setup.

Hypothesis: The permission boundary was tightened to require either a specific resource tag or a caller principal condition. Terraform provider calls that do not set the tag fail. Older roles created before the boundary are unaffected, new role attachments fail.
Verified GCP side (for cross-cloud workflows) is unaffected; this is AWS-specific.

Checked linked internal ticket INT-951357 (similar boundary enforcement), but that ticket dealt with CI service account tagging; current issue is terraform-runner cannot surface the required tag when calling IAM APIs.

Temporary mitigation tested: manually create the EC2 role and instance profile using a human operator with elevated perms, then let terraform import the resources. This allows pipeline to continue but is manual and not scalable.
workaround: Manual creation of role & instance profile by ops (with elevated user that bypasses the boundary), then terraform import to unlock workspace. For queued pipelines, ops can create temporary roles to unblock. Documented in runbook 'priv-deploy/mitigations-2026-03'.
